major_error_concepts: Assuming every unseen marked individual is dead rather than undetected or outside the sampled area.

cards.prompt: What is Detection Probability? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
cards.definition: Detection probability is the chance of observing a target conditional on its presence under the sampling process. It can vary by species, observer, habitat, and effort, so nondetection is not identical to confirmed absence.
required_concepts: Observation is conditional on presence and an imperfect detection process.
major_error_concepts: Equating zero observations with certain absence regardless of effort.

cards.prompt: What is Occupancy Model? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
cards.definition: Occupancy models estimate occurrence while accounting for imperfect detection using an explicit repeated-observation structure and assumptions. Estimated occupancy differs from the raw fraction of sites with detections and does not directly measure abundance without further modeling.
required_concepts: Presence inference separates occurrence from detection.
major_error_concepts: Treating occupancy probability as the expected number of individuals at a site.

cards.prompt: What is Before-After-Control-Impact? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
cards.definition: A before-after-control-impact design compares changes at impacted and control locations over time to strengthen inference about an intervention or disturbance. Baseline comparability, replication, and differing background trends still matter; the design label alone does not remove every confounder.
required_concepts: Comparative temporal changes help distinguish impact from background variation.
major_error_concepts: Assuming any one before-and-after comparison without a control is a full BACI study.

cards.prompt: What is Ecological Experiment? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
cards.definition: An ecological experiment manipulates a factor and compares outcomes under a design suited to the scale of the process. Randomization, controls, independent replication, and spillover considerations determine what causal conclusions the experiment can support.
required_concepts: Manipulation requires design matched to ecological scale and interference.
major_error_concepts: Assuming any manipulated plot proves landscape-wide effects regardless of scale or replication.

cards.prompt: What is Pseudoreplication? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
cards.definition: Pseudoreplication occurs when observations are treated as independent replicates of a treatment or process even though the relevant experimental units are not independently replicated. Repeated measurements can improve information without supplying independent treatment replication.
required_concepts: Observation count differs from independent experimental-unit count.
major_error_concepts: Counting many measurements from one treated watershed as many independent treated watersheds.

cards.prompt: What is Remote Sensing? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
cards.definition: Remote sensing observes ecological properties indirectly through signals measured at a distance. Spatial resolution, timing, calibration, and ground-based evidence determine what properties can be inferred; a spectral signal is not automatically a direct species census.
required_concepts: Remote measurements require a justified link to the ecological quantity.
major_error_concepts: Treating vegetation greenness alone as an exact count of species or total ecosystem health.

cards.prompt: What is Conservation Prioritization? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
cards.definition: Conservation prioritization allocates limited effort among explicit objectives and constraints using ecological evidence and stated values. Different goals can favor different actions, so a priority score is a decision framework rather than a universal biological ranking.
required_concepts: Limited-resource decisions require explicit objectives, tradeoffs, and evidence.
major_error_concepts: Claiming one numerical score objectively maximizes every possible conservation goal.

description: A definition-recall course deck covering core concepts in Ecology.
